newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-PARMA PROVE THAT THERE IS LIFE AFTER ZOLA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PARMA PROVE THAT THERE IS LIFE AFTER ZOLA.

text.p: English soccer fans may find it hard to believe but Italian serie A side Parma have proved that there is life after Gianfranco Zola.
Last November Parma sprang a major surprise in agreeing to sell Italy international Zola to English premier league side Chelsea.
Many Italian commentators bemoaned the export of so flamboyantly Mediterranean a talent as Sardinian-born Zola, arguing that in rejecting him Parma had turned their back on instinctive flair.
Zola has carried all before him in a brilliantly successful first season in England. Chelsea have reached the F.A. Cup final while the player himself has been voted Footballer of the Year.
In the meantime, however, Parma have moved up the serie A table, rising from the relegation zone to second place, four points behind leaders Juventus with four games to play.
Parma coach Carlo Ancelotti appears to have landed a long-range gamble with his decision last autumn to prefer 21-year-old Argentine Hernan Crespo to Zola in attack.
Ancelotti is a firm believer in a hard-working 4-4-2 line-up which tended to cramp Zola's style while requiring the qualities of a central target man such as Crespo in attack.
After a difficult beginning in his first season in Italian soccer, Crespo has developed a useful understanding with Enrico Chiesa, Parma's $15 million buy last summer.
On Sunday Crespo scored all Parma's goals in an emphatic 3-0 home win over against Vicenza, a result which maintains the pressure on leaders Juventus.
With 11 goals to his credit, Crespo is beginning to look well worth the $3.5 million Parma paid Argentine club River Plate for him last summer.
However, Crespo struck a modest note after Sunday's game, saying: "I've got a lot to learn, I haven't become a phenomenon just because I've scored three goals."
With the Italian calendar rescheduled, Parma now have a difficult home game against AC Milan on Thursday three days before whazt could be a decisive clash with Juventus in Turin next Sunday.
"The championship is still wide open, we're still in there...but on Thursday we'll need all the help we can get from the fans," said coach Ancelotti.
Juventus, 2-0 away winners over Verona on Sunday, are at home to relegation battlers Piacenza on Thursday.
Juventus coach Marcello Lippi was not unduly troubled by Sunday's results.

"We wanted and still want to arrive at the direct clash (with Parma) with our four-point lead intact...Another game is behind us and we're still four points clear and now it's next stop Piacenza on Thursday," he said.
Even if, as seems likely, Parma lose their championship battle against Juventus they can take consolation from the form shown by Crespo.
With room for improvement, the young Argentine seems destined to prove that life at Parma, even without Zola, can be successful.
